title: Potential Energy, Conservation of Energy and Power

items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A water-park puzzle opens the lesson: three slides from the same height, a boy and his father at the top.

Balls dropped into sand show a raised object **stores energy**; lifting a box gives **U = mgh**. A falling ball tracked at four points shows U turning into K while **K + U stays the same**, giving **v = √(2gh)**.

Two students climbing the same stairs introduce **power, P = W ÷ t**, with the watt, kilowatt and horsepower.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• work done, W = F × s, and the joule

• weight of an object, mg

• kinetic energy, K = ½mv², and the work–energy theorem

• the equation of motion v² = u² + 2as

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Calculate gravitational potential energy (mgh).

**2.** Apply conservation of mechanical energy to a falling body.

**3.** Calculate power and convert units (watt, kilowatt, horsepower).

chunks.name: Where does the energy come from?

items.text:
**Answer to Question 6**

From the **work done in lifting it**. That work was stored in the ball because of its raised position.

script.x: Question 6, with the three drops in view. Answer is on pointer 1.
Show the key idea on potential energy.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A box of mass m lifted **slowly** (without speeding up) from the ground through a height **h**. Its weight, mg, acts down; the lifting force F acts up.

**Answer to Question 7**

A force **equal to its weight**, **F = mg**, upwards.

**Answer to Question 8**

W = F × s = mg × h = **mgh**.

**Answer to Question 9**

It is **stored in the box** as gravitational potential energy.

items.prompt: A 200 g cricket ball is thrown straight up and reaches 10 m above the ground. Its potential energy at the highest point is (g = 10 m/s²)

Fill in the blanks: a 50 kg student goes from the ground to the top of a 20 m building, once by lift and once by the stairs. The gain in potential energy is ____ J by lift and ____ J by the stairs. (g = 10 m/s²)
A book on a shelf at height h has potential energy U. If it is moved to a shelf at height 3h, its potential energy becomes

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: 200 g = 0.2 kg. U = 0.2 × 10 × 10 = **20 J**. (B) forgets to convert grams.

**On Question 2**

**A**: U = 50 × 10 × 20 = **10 000 J** in both cases: it depends only on the **height**, not the path.

**On Question 3**

**C**: U ∝ h, so three times the height gives **three times** the potential energy.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A **1 kg** ball dropped from rest at A, **20 m** up, passing B (15 m), C (5 m) and D (just before it lands). g = 10 m/s².

**Answer to Question 10**

U = 1 × 10 × 20 = **200 J**; K = 0. So U + K = **200 J**.

**Answer to Question 13**

It is **200 J at every point**. U falls by exactly as much as K rises.

items.text:
**What this shows**

**Figure 1** (left): an object of mass m at rest at **position 1**, a height h above the ground.

**Figure 2** (right, revealed after Question 14): after falling a distance s, it is at **position 2**, a height h′ above the ground.

**Answer to Question 14**

u = 0, so K = ½mu² = **0**, and U = **mgh**. So K + U = **mgh**.

**Answer to Question 15**

K + U = **½mv² + mgh′**.

**Answer to Question 16**

u = 0 and a = g, so **v² = 2gs**.

**Answer to Question 17**

K + U = ½m(2gs) + mgh′. From the figure, **s = h − h′**, so K + U = mg(h − h′) + mgh′ = **mgh**.

**Answer to Question 18**

K + U = mgh at **both** positions. Position 2 can be any point on the way down, so **K + U is constant** at any position.

**Answer to Question 19**

½mv² = mgh, so v² = 2gh and **v = √(2gh)**.

items.text:
**Answer to Question 20**

**No and no**: m cancels, and only the height h appears. Ignoring friction, the boy and his father reach the bottom of **any** of the three slides with the **same speed**.

script.x: Question 20 settles the hook. Answer is on pointer 1.
Show the key idea: the conservation of mechanical energy.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A pendulum bob released from **P**. It swings down through **Q**, the lowest point, and up to **R**.

**Answer to Question 21**

**U** is greatest at **P and R**, the highest points, where the bob stops for an instant. **K** is greatest at **Q**, the lowest point.

**Answer to Question 22**

Its mechanical energy is **conserved**: the K it has at Q turns back into U.

**Answer to Question 23**

**Air resistance and friction** at the support turn its mechanical energy into heat, bit by bit.

items.prompt: A stone is dropped from a cliff 45 m high. Ignoring air resistance, its speed just before it hits the ground is (g = 10 m/s²)
A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. Its kinetic energy when it is 4 m above the ground is (g = 10 m/s²)
True or false? When a ball thrown straight up reaches its highest point, its kinetic energy is zero and its potential energy is the greatest.
options: True: all its K has turned into U
False: its K is greatest at the top
False: both are zero at the top
True: but K + U is now greater

items.text:
**On Question 2**

**B**: it has fallen 6 m, so K = U lost = 2 × 10 × 6 = **120 J**. (A) is its U at 4 m.

**On Question 3**

**A**: **true**. It stops for an instant at the top, so all its K has turned into U.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Left: a boy runs up stairs **6 m** high in **10 s**.

• Right: a girl walks up the same stairs in **40 s**.

**Answer to Question 24**

**Neither.** Each does W = mgh = 50 × 10 × 6 = **3000 J**.

**Answer to Question 25**

The boy does the same work in **less time**. He works faster.

**Answer to Question 26**

Boy: 3000 ÷ 10 = **300 J** every second. Girl: 3000 ÷ 40 = **75 J** every second.

items.prompt: A crane lifts a 500 kg load through 12 m in 20 s. Its power is (g = 10 m/s²)
A crane lifts a load to the 10th floor of a building. It then lifts the same load to the 20th floor in twice the time. Compared with the first lift, the second lift needs
options: twice the energy and twice the power
twice the energy and the same power
the same energy and half the power
four times the energy and twice the power

items.prompt: A car engine is rated 120 hp. Its power in kilowatts is about

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: W = 500 × 10 × 12 = 60 000 J. P = 60 000 ÷ 20 = 3000 W = **3 kW**. (B) forgets to divide by the time.

**On Question 2**

**B**: twice the height needs **twice the work**, done in twice the time, so P = W ÷ t stays **the same**.
